extracted.intended_audience: users of plain TeX / macro writers and typesetters implementing documents in plain.tex
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, conventions, and practical rules for using and writing macros in plain TeX (plain.tex), including spacing, alignment, page output, math macros, and character-code considerations. Intended for people writing TeX documents or extending/using plain.tex macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakable vs non-breakable horizontal spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\enskip, \\quad, and \\qquad for spaces that are legitimate breakpoints within a paragraph; use \\enspace, \\thinspace, and \\negthinspace for spaces that cannot cause a break. All six of these spaces are relative to the current font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one of these macros depending on whether you want the space to permit line breaks. The macros are font-relative; prefer them over hard kerns when you want typographic-appropriate spacing that respects breaking rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent (glue) horizontal and vertical space
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\hglue (defined as an afterassignment form) to get horizontal space that never disappears and is able to stretch or shrink; use \\vglue as the vertical analog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For horizontal glue that should persist regardless of adjacent breaks, use the \\hglue form. For vertical glue that must persist, use \\vglue. Example notation in plain.tex: ‘\\hgluehgluei’ and ‘\\vgluehgluei’.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppressing interline glue
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\nointerlineskip to suppress interline glue that would ordinarily be inserted before the next box in vertical mode; use \\offinterlineskip to set things so that future interline glue will be present but zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \\nointerlineskip for a one-shot suppression before a particular box; use \\offinterlineskip when you need a more drastic setting affecting subsequent lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical breakable spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\smallskip, \\medskip, and \\bigskip to insert potentially breakable vertical spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These macros insert vertical glues of preset amounts and are intended where vertical breaks and flexible spacing are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty and break macros usage by mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\break, \\nobreak, and \\allowbreak in any mode; use ~ (tie) and \\slash in horizontal mode; other penalty macros that begin with \\par are intended only for vertical mode (between paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the appropriate break/penalty macro according to current mode (horizontal vs vertical). E.g., ~ and \\slash are for horizontal mode; vertical-mode penalties begin with \\par.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of boxing macros for line/full-width and zero-width boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\line, \\leftline, \\rightline, and \\centerline to produce boxes of the full line width; use \\llap and \\rlap to make boxes whose effective width is zero. Use \\underbar to put an argument into an hbox with a straight line at fixed distance under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick the macro that matches the desired horizontal behavior: full-line boxes for titles/lines, llap/rlap for overlapping zero-width boxes; \\underbar uses math mode internally to position the line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include \relax when macros may appear first in alignment entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a leading \\relax in macros like \\strut because TeX is in a somewhat unpredictable mode when a macro appears first in an alignment entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defining macros that might start an alignment cell, add a \\relax to avoid unexpected behavior. The text illustrates this with the \\strut macro ('\\relax...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \ialign when initial \tabskip must be zero; use \hidewidth and \multispan for alignment control
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\ialign to ensure \\tabskip is initially zero. Use \\hidewidth where entries may stick out of their column and \\multispan to span columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building alignments that rely on exact tabskip behavior, prefer \\ialign. Use \\multispan{n} to omit n-1 column separators and glue together columns; use \\hidewidth to emulate \\hfill inside alignment entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and test tabbing macros interactively
rubrics_metrics.description: The tabbing macros are complicated; 'The best way to understand these macros is probably to watch them in action on simple examples, using \\tracingall.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When learning or debugging \\settabs/\\tabalign behavior, run simple examples with tracing enabled (\\tracingall or other tracing commands) to observe tokenization/alignment and detect stray arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \+ (outer) vs \tabalign (non-outer) appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The macro \\+ has been declared '\\outer' so that TeX can better detect runaway arguments; a non-\\outer version \\tabalign is provided for use in inner contexts. You can use \\tabalign just like \\+ except after \\settabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a macro must be protected from being used in inner contexts or to detect runaway arguments, use the outer form; if you need the macro inside other macros/arguments, use the non-outer alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph-shape helpers and their behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\hang to cause hanging indentation by \\parindent after the first line; use \\textindent{stuff} to put 'stuff' into the indentation (flush right except for an en space) and to remove spaces that might follow the right brace. \\item, \\itemitem, and \\narrower provide paragraph shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For list-like paragraph shapes use \\item or \\itemitem. Use \\textindent{...} to inject deliberate indent content at paragraph start; it also removes following spaces that could otherwise appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to use \beginsection
rubrics_metrics.description: Invoke \\beginsection as ‘\\beginsection<section title>’ followed by a blank line (or \\par). The macro emits glue and penalties to encourage a page break if the page is nearly full, inserts a \\bigskip, prints the title flush left in bold, displays the title on the terminal, then does a \\smallskip with page break prohibited and issues a \\noindent so the next paragraph is not indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the title and then a blank line to start the section properly. Be aware that if vertical-mode material immediately follows \\beginsection the next 'paragraph' may be empty; the macro also manages page-breaking behavior for section starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \proclaim for theorems/ proclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\proclaim #1. #2\\par to typeset special statements (theorems, lemmas, definitions...). It puts the proclamation title in boldface, sets the rest of the paragraph in slanted type, and follows the paragraph with a break similar to \\medbreak but with a penalty adjusted so page breaks are discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \\proclaim is intended to give consistent typographic treatment for mathematical proclamations; it also affects page break penalties so proclaim environments are less likely to be split across pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ragged-right setting: prerequisites and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not call \\raggedright until your text font has already been specified; the macro assumes ragged-right material will not be in a variety of different sizes. If material uses different sizes, set \\fontdimen parameters 3 and 4 of the relevant fonts to zero (e.g., ‘\\fontdimen3\\tenrm=0pt’) to remove interword stretch/shrink. Use \\ttraggedright for ragged-right in typewriter font (typewriter spaces are already unstretchable and unshrinkable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure font selection precedes \\raggedright. For heterogeneous-size ragged-right text, adjust fontdimen3/4 rather than relying on \\raggedright. For monospaced type use \\ttraggedright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \leavevmode to start a paragraph when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\leavevmode before constructions that build up a symbol by forming a box: it begins a paragraph if TeX is in vertical mode, but does nothing in horizontal or math mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert \\leavevmode in macros that must operate in horizontal mode but might be invoked at the start of vertical mode to guarantee expected behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended way to end a plain.tex document
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\bye defined as ‘\\outer\\def\\bye{\\par\\vfill\\supereject\\end}’ — the recommended way to stop a plain.tex job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminate plain TeX documents with \\bye (not with abrupt end-of-file) to ensure proper final page output and the supereject behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math spacing and prime-notation helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\sp and \\sb as alternatives to ^ and _. Use \\, \\!, \\>, and \\; for thin/negative/medium/thick math spacing. Active-character tricks in plain.tex convert sequences like f'''' into f^{\\prime\\prime\\prime}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These macros provide more convenient typing alternatives and fine control over spacing in math; prefer them when readability or keyboard limitations make ^ / _ / explicit \mskip commands awkward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided macros for common multi-style constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\mathpalette to build constructs that behave correctly in all four math styles; macros like \\phantom, \\smash, and \\root use \\mathpalette. Note: \\phantom and \\smash assume the current style is uncramped and therefore are not perfect in every situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing macros that must adapt to display/text/script/scriptscript styles, base them on \\mathpalette. Be aware of limitations such as assumptions about cramping; test in all styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided delimiters and size macros for scalable delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 24 delimiters and the \\big/\\Big/... family to produce delimiters of specified sizes; the big macros implement fixed sizes for \\big, \\Big, \\bigg, \\Bigg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer these macros over manual sizing when you need consistent delimiter sizing. For truly extensible delimiters, use the delimiter primitives as wrapped by these macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix and bordermatrix usage for consistent alignment and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\matrix{...} to ensure two n-rowed matrices have the same height and depth unless rows are unusually big. Use \\bordermatrix when a labeled matrix with border is needed; it uses a constant \\p@renwd representing the width of a big left parenthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on \\matrix for typical matrix typesetting to get consistent vertical dimensions; prefer \\bordermatrix for labeled matrices but be aware of its more complex internal assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed-equation alignments and spacing assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\eqalign, \\eqalignno, \\leqalignno, and \\displaylines for various kinds of displayed equation alignment. The \\displ@y macro opens up baselines via \\openup and manages \\everycr so inter-display line penalties and baseline spacing are handled correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided alignment macros for consistent displayed-math formatting; understand that \\lineskiplimit and open-up amounts affect spacing so keep these defaults unless you intentionally alter them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page output and header/footer control
rubrics_metrics.description: Control page numbering and headers/footers via \\pageno, \\headline, and \\footline. Use \\nopagenumbers to blank out the footline; \\advancepageno increments page numbers in a sign-aware way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set \\headline and \\footline token registers to control running heads and footers; use \\nopagenumbers when page numbers should be suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote insertion behavior and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\footnote and \\vfootnote which rely on \\insert ootins and set parameters like \\splittopskip, \\splitmaxdepth and \\floatingpenalty; these macros avoid requiring the footnote text as a parameter to the insertion macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the provided footnote machinery manage splitting and top-baseline for broken footnotes; if customizing footnote behavior, adjust the relevant registers carefully (\\splittopskip, \\splitmaxdepth, \\floatingpenalty, \\skip\\footins, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating insertions: top/mid/page insertion macros and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \\topinsert, \\midinsert, \\pageinsert to create floating material. Various parameters control their behavior: \\skip\\topins, \\count\\topins, \\dimen\\topins, and \\floatingpenalty. The \\endinsert routine evaluates whether a mid-insert should be converted to a top insert depending on page goal and page total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the insertion registers' magnification, skip, and dimension limits when placing floats; for predictable float behavior set these registers appropriately and be aware of how mid/page/top distinction affects placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \tracingall / \loggingall to debug complex macro behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: For debugging macros, alignments, and output routines, use \\tracingall or \\loggingall to enable extensive tracing of commands, paragraphs, macros, outputs, and showbox parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tracking down subtle macro or alignment bugs, enable tracing to see token expansion and box/list construction; remember to disable it after debugging because it produces voluminous output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation minima and loading patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Set \\lefthyphenmin and \\righthyphenmin (plain.tex sets them to 2 and 3 respectively) to disallow one-letter or two-letter fragments at hyphenation boundaries. Plain.tex reads hyphenation patterns via ‘\\input hyphen’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust \\lefthyphenmin and \\righthyphenmin if you need different hyphenation behavior for a language or special typography; otherwise use the defaults to avoid poor hyphenation like x- or -xx breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEX's internal character code and portability rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: TEX converts external character representations to a standard internal code based on ASCII (codes 0..127) when reading files and converts back when writing. This makes TeX constructions portable across machines; e.g., alphabetic constants like ‘'b’ denote the integer 98 in ASCII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing macros or handling character codes, assume plain TeX's internal ASCII-based codes for portability. Use ASCII conventions when referring to character numeric values and be cautious about host-specific encodings at file I/O boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify plain.tex except for preloaded fonts without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Macro files like plain.tex should not be changed in any way, except with respect to preloaded fonts, unless the changes are authorized by the author of the macros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid altering plain.tex internals; if adjustments are required, prefer loading local macro files or adjusting only font preload settings. Changes to core macros can create compatibility/support problems.
